Hi Aditya + Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. Attached are Acme's redlines to the MSA + Order Form. Our legal team pushed back primarily on the damage exclusion language: they want a one-way consequential exclusion (no liability to us for lost profits, incidental/special/punitive), but they want an explicit carve-out for IP infringement and gross negligence.

Two specific asks from Acme legal:
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept a mutual consequential-exclusion (mutual = neither party recovers special/incidental/consequential damages) instead of Acme's proposed one-way.
- Clarify the definition bucket: Acme interprets "consequential" to include lost profits and third-party claims tied to data loss. They want a tighter definition so client-side data-loss claims can be excluded from the exclusion.

Please see attached PDF for line-by-line. Procurement is tracking this alongside our SOW schedule — we need a decision this week to keep our go-live target.

Best,
Marta Sanchez
Senior Counsel, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Analytics

Laura / Sergio — looping you both in to coordinate the response to Acme. Marta, thanks for the packet. High-level notes from commercial: Acme is a priority pilot; we want to avoid blocking the deal over wording if we can find a pragmatic compromise.

From a sales perspective the main items to preserve are:
- A clear cap on liability tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months (or a fixed dollar cap if we must).
- A mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages is preferred (keeps symmetry).
- Maintain carve-outs for IP infringement, willful misconduct/gross negligence, and validated indemnities.

Can legal propose a short mutual exclusion with a definitional schedule that limits "consequential" to indirect economic losses and excludes third-party indemnity claims tied to Redwood's breach of data handling? If we can do that, procurement is likely to accept.

Sergio — can you draft a proposal and flag any items that require leadership signoff/crediting?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marta Sanchez <marta.sanchez@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form — damages exclusions (redlines attached)

Thanks Aditya — attaching a concise redline and suggested language. I recommend we start with mutual exclusion language but add narrow carve-outs so Acme keeps protection for data-loss-related third-party claims. Proposal below (insert into Order Form "Limitation of Liability" section):

--- Suggested mutual exclusion (short form) ---
"Except for (a) damages arising from a party's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) obligations under the indemnification provisions for intellectual property infringement; (c) Customer's payment obligations; and (d) personal injury or death, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, punitive or exemplary damages, including lost profits, loss of business or loss of data, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability or otherwise, even if advised of the possibility of such damages."

--- Definition addendum (to reduce definition fight) ---
"For clarity, 'loss of data' as used above shall be limited to the loss of Customer-provided data for which Redwood has demonstrable breach of its data handling obligations under the Agreement. Third-party claims arising out of Customer data loss that are covered by the indemnity provisions shall be recoverable notwithstanding the foregoing exclusion."

Rationale: this is mutual (commercial balance), preserves core carve-outs (IP indemnity, gross negligence), and narrows the 'loss of data' language to avoid Acme's request to treat all data-related downstream losses as excluded from the exclusion (which would effectively expand their recoverability).

Open items:
- Cap level: propose 12 months' fees or $2M, whichever is greater — need commercial sign-off.
- Punitive damages: Redwood historically excludes punitive except where required by law; propose 'to the extent allowed by applicable law' carve-in for punitive damages.

Attachment: proposed-liability-snippet.docx (Word, 8KB)

Sergio, Aditya — thank you for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. Acme legal reviewed the mutual phrasing and the definition addendum. A few clarifying items before we can mark this as final:

1) The definition addendum helps, but Acme needs assurance that 'demonstrable breach of data handling obligations' does not require us to perform forensic proof beyond a reasonable standard. Can Redwood agree to 'a preponderance of evidence or findings in a mutually agreed forensic report'?

2) Cap: procurement requests a flat cap of $3,000,000 for the Order Form (our internal limit for pilot engagements). Would Redwood accept $3M rather than a months-based formula?

3) Punitive damages: Acme still prefers explicit carve-out language stating punitive/exemplary damages are excluded unless required by applicable law. Your parenthetical suggestion aligns with ours; can you include the exact phrasing we can redline?

If we can get (1) and (3) resolved, procurement is comfortable with the $3M cap and will close the SOW review. Looking forward to your short confirmation so our procurement lead can issue the PO.
